clue.text: Family cold to lubbers, except daughter

definitions.note: a collective noun used for the members of a clan, a plural answer

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the word for lubbers

parts.note: landlubbers, people who live on land rather than at sea, are landsmen
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A family turns chilly towards a group of landlubbers, except for one daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a clan form one extended kin group, so the people in it stand for a whole family.

clue.text: In jest send up inexperienced song-writer

indicators.note: In tells us to put the reversed piece inside the word for jest

parts.note: cod as a noun or adjective means a hoax or joke

indicators.note: in a down clue send up asks for the word to be read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: raw means green or inexperienced, as a raw recruit

explanation.surface: Someone, as a joke, mocks a novice composer of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send up' turns the word for inexperienced upside down. Noël Coward wrote songs such as Mad Dogs and Englishmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward, the English playwright, also wrote and composed many popular songs.

clue.text: Political system gives a role to head of the Scots

parts.note: a part is a role played by an actor
heid is the Scots dialect word for head

explanation.surface: A political arrangement hands a part to the leader of the Scottish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of the Scots' looks like a first-letter instruction, but it asks for the Scots word for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was the system of racial segregation enforced by South Africa's government.

clue.text: Trained to use poles, up valley

parts.note: to ski is to travel using ski poles

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: Someone is taught to use sticks while climbing a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DELL into LLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trained in a craft has acquired expertise, so is skilled at it.

clue.text: Ferrara family runs to fat

parts.note: the House of Este ruled the Italian city of Ferrara in the Renaissance
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A noble Italian dynasty gets plump over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats are chemically a kind of this compound, made from glycerol and fatty acids, so it loosely stands for fat.

clue.text: Prepare to become a mummy

parts.note: looks like a woman getting ready for motherhood, but means preserving a corpse

explanation.surface: An expectant woman readies herself for motherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians preserved bodies with spices and resins to make mummies.

clue.text: Mark, one superior to king, is to assume old kingdom

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
in a suit of cards the ace ranks above the king
to don clothes is to put them on, to assume them

explanation.surface: Mark, a man above the king, is to take over an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was the ancient Greek realm of Philip II and Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Mad Lear, one role in Shakespeare

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters going wildly astray and being rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: King Lear in his madness is a single part in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges LEAR plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in The Tempest.

clue.text: Religious circle pray finally you'll come back here?

parts.note: a mandala is a circular symbol of the universe in Hindu and Buddhist religion

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word pray

explanation.surface: After praying in a sacred circle, you will return to this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Kipling's poem 'Mandalay', with its refrain 'Come you back to Mandalay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem invites the listener to come back to this Burmese city.

clue.text: Unrepeatable performance? Note, it's been put in twice before

indicators.note: put in means the note is placed inside the pair of words for before

parts.note: pre and ere both mean before, giving two words
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A one-off show is described as having a musical note set into it twice before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice before' gives two different words for before, and the note sits between them; a premiere happens only once, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A first night happens only once, so the opening performance of a work can never be repeated.

clue.text: Basic force from all of us alike putting energy into steady pull

parts.note: we refers to all of us together
akin means similar or alike

indicators.note: putting with into tells us to place the energy symbol inside the pull
into marks where the letter for energy goes, inside the word for pull

parts.note: traction is the act of pulling a load steadily
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A fundamental force arises from us all being similar and adding energy to a steady pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' ... 'into' places E in TRACTION, giving TERACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics names four fundamental forces, one of which governs radioactive beta decay.

clue.text: Snake that makes one frightened

definitions.meaning: a rattlesnake is known informally by this name
something that rattles you unnerves you

explanation.surface: A snake that scares you.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is nicknamed for its rattling tail, and anything that rattles a person alarms them.

clue.text: This person, sounding more stupid, gets a bit of brain

parts.note: the setter calls themself this person, which is me

indicators.note: sounding means the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: duller means less bright, more stupid

explanation.surface: Someone sounding thicker gains a little brain matter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent DULLER is said like DULLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The medulla oblongata is the lowest part of the brainstem.

clue.text: Such fuel boy got for nothing round back of store

indicators.note: round means the boy goes around the letter from store

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of store

parts.note: free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A lad bought petrol free of charge from round the back of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives E from 'store', and 'round' sets it inside LAD to give LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded petrol has no added tetraethyl lead, so it is described this way.

clue.text: Criticise, say, London greed

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise
London is an example of a city, so say, London means a city

explanation.surface: Attack the avarice of, for example, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping, insatiable greed.

clue.text: Any stranger may come to city as one of a herd

indicators.note: stranger means more odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Any outsider can come to town as one of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' rearranges ANY into NYA.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is an African antelope that lives in herds.

clue.text: Like chap to suppress one slander

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one goes inside

parts.note: a chap is a person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: It's like a man to stifle a single defamatory remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suppress' puts I inside PERSON, giving PERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast an aspersion is to make a damaging, defamatory remark.

clue.text: Place I start to claim in one college is unreserved

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in tells us these letters go inside one plus a college

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
PL is the abbreviation for place in street names

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of claim

explanation.surface: I begin to stake a claim at a place in one college, completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives C from 'claim'; PLIC goes inside I and MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit trust or faith is complete and without any reservation.

clue.text: Red Dwarf introducing himself?

indicators.note: a speaker introducing himself puts me before his name

parts.note: the dwarf speaking of himself would say me
Doc is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: One of Snow White's dwarfs presents himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Doc introducing himself says 'Me, Doc'.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a Bordeaux region whose red wines are known by its name.

clue.text: Eat an ice, swallowing quantity

indicators.note: swallowing means the cone takes the quantity inside it

parts.note: an ice-cream cone is an ice
a sum is an amount or quantity

explanation.surface: Eat an ice cream, gulping a good amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an ice' is a British term for an ice cream, here served in a cone.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to eat it.

clue.text: Vigorous exercise as journalists swallow drink

indicators.note: swallow means the journalists take the drink inside

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
to sup is to drink, and a sup is a drink

explanation.surface: Hard workouts as reporters down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Press-ups are what Americans call push-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ups are a strenuous exercise of raising the body with the arms.

clue.text: Crusoe supposedly raised dagger to catch deer

indicators.note: to catch means the dagger holds the deer inside it
in a down clue raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade
an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Crusoe raised a dagger to trap a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the dagger upwards, giving SIRK, which takes the deer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Selkirk, a marooned Scottish sailor, was the likely model for Defoe's Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Blacksmith who makes a lot of money?

definitions.meaning: one who works metal at a forge

definitions.text: who makes a lot of money?
definitions.meaning: a counterfeiter who prints fake banknotes

explanation.surface: A smith who earns a fortune?
explanation.definitionFit: A smith shapes metal at a forge, while a counterfeiter fakes banknotes, literally making money.

clue.text: Left a section of few words

parts.note: a conic section is a curve cut from a cone, so conic follows section here

explanation.surface: Someone left a part that is brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' is used for CONIC through the phrase 'conic section'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laconic person speaks tersely, using very few words.

clue.text: My beer left unfinished — it's sort of pink

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: left unfinished means the beer loses its final letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: My beer was left half-drunk, and it is a pinkish colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left unfinished' cuts ALE to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour named after the sea creature's skeleton.

clue.text: Not so bright, second city

parts.note: paler means less bright
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Less brilliant, the second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital city of Sicily.

clue.text: Essentially, the other Alexandre Dumas overshadowed son

indicators.note: overshadowed means the father covers the son, holding him inside

parts.note: the novelist Alexandre Dumas père was father of the playwright Alexandre Dumas fils

explanation.surface: Essentially, the elder Dumas eclipsed his son.
explanation.walkthrough: The two writers were father and son, so 'the other' is père, the father. S goes inside PERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by or in itself, intrinsically, so essentially.

clue.text: Pouring on to course —- time for exercise

indicators.note: on to means the first piece is added after the course and time

parts.note: a circuit is a racecourse or track
pouring with rain is raining

explanation.surface: It starts teeming on the racecourse, so time for a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fitness regime of rotating through a series of exercise stations.

clue.text: Shoot old girl in boat's bar

definitions.meaning: a shoot springing from the base of a plant, as in grasses and cereals
the ... Girls were a famous British dance troupe of high-kicking chorus girls, so one of them is an old girl
the lever used to turn a boat's rudder

explanation.surface: Fire at a former girlfriend in the bar on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition with 'in' as a link. The Tiller Girls were precision dancers seen on British stage and television through the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a plant's side stem, a dancer from the Tiller troupe, and a helm lever.

clue.text: On being arrested, saboteur lost his head, I think

indicators.note: being arrested means the word on is held inside the saboteur
lost his head means the saboteur's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a wrecker sabotages things

explanation.surface: Once arrested, the saboteur panicked, I believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his head' removes the W from WRECKER, and 'being arrested' sets ON inside the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reckons judges or supposes, so whoever says 'I think' is acting as one.
